abstract: I'm a machine learning engineer, working mostly on healthcare and finance. I started out in electronics (an IEEE paper and a patent), then moved into machine learning and data science at the University of Maryland, where I also worked as a data scientist at the Counseling Center Research Unit. Recently I built ClinIQ, a patient-triage assistant for small clinics, at the Anthropic Hackathon.

projects.name: Book Recommender
projects.question: Recommends books similar to ones a reader already liked.
projects.method: Finds books that readers rated in similar ways, then tests how many look-alike books to compare.
projects.result: Most accurate when comparing 15 similar books (average error of 1.28 rating points).

projects.name: Medical Chatbot on AWS
projects.question: Takes a medical chatbot from a notebook to a live website.
projects.method: A chatbot that answers medical questions from a document database, packaged with Docker and redeployed to AWS automatically on every code change.
projects.result: Each code push goes live on AWS automatically. The bot remembers the conversation and is monitored.
projects.stack: Python · LangChain · Pinecone · OpenAI · Flask · Docker · AWS · GitHub Actions

projects.name: Private Medical Chatbot
projects.question: A medical Q&A chatbot that keeps patient data on your own computer.
projects.method: An open-source AI model runs on the local machine. It searches medical PDFs before answering, declines off-topic questions and skips weak matches.
projects.result: No patient information is sent to any outside service.
projects.stack: Python · Ollama · ChromaDB · Hugging Face · Flask · Docker

projects.name: Watt's Next?
projects.question: Predicts how far electric cars will go and where new chargers are needed.
projects.method: Analysed 216,772 electric-vehicle records from Washington State with regression, classification, clustering and maps (with a co-author).
projects.result: Predicted electric driving range with R² = 0.918.

projects.name: Sentimental Liquidity
projects.question: Uses the tone of Federal Reserve statements to improve a bank's interest-rate risk model.
projects.method: Claude rates each Fed statement from dovish to hawkish (1–10). That one number nudges a standard interest-rate model, which simulates 1,000 possible futures; a second model estimates how many depositors would leave in each.
projects.result: A Value-at-Risk report for a simulated $10B bank. The AI provides one score, and everything else is standard math.
projects.stack: Python · Claude API · NumPy · SciPy · scikit-learn

projects.name: TravelGenie
projects.question: Plans a whole trip from one request.
projects.method: Claude coordinates seven small tools (flights, hotels, events, maps, weather, currency, traffic), with a web app and a Slack bot on top.
projects.result: One request becomes a day-by-day itinerary with a budget. Team project.
projects.stack: Python · Claude API · MCP · Streamlit · Slack

projects.name: ClinIQ
projects.question: Helps doctors at under-resourced clinics decide which patients to see first.
projects.method: Ranks patients with a simple, transparent point score. A local AI model then writes a summary for the doctor and a plain-language one for the patient, answering only from a medical encyclopedia and FDA drug labels. A three-step check flags unsafe prescriptions.
projects.result: Built at the Anthropic Hackathon (Health & Wellbeing track). If the medical knowledge base is missing, the AI features turn off.

projects.name: This profile
projects.question: Uses AI to keep this page up to date, with checks so it can't make things up.
projects.method: Every Monday a GitHub Action collects my public activity and Claude writes a short update. Code checks every project name and number against the real data; if anything doesn't match, it gets one retry, then a plain automatic summary.
projects.result: Every weekly update can be traced back to real activity.

chunks.text: I'm a machine learning engineer, working mostly on healthcare and finance. I started out in electronics (an IEEE paper and a patent), then moved into machine learning and data science at the University of Maryland, where I also worked as a data scientist at the Counseling Center Research Unit. Recently I built ClinIQ, a patient-triage assistant for small clinics, at the Anthropic Hackathon.
What I do: Chatbots that answer from real documents, AI that uses tools, and machine learning for finance and healthcare
Background: Electronics: an IEEE paper on 160 GHz amplifiers for 5G and satellites, and a patent for a child-safety wearable
Studied: Machine learning & data science, University of Maryland

Worked: Data Scientist, UMD Counseling Center Research Unit: a campus-wide survey on food access and student well-being, presented to UMD's Vice President of Student Affairs and at the Maryland Student Affairs Conference
Highlights: ClinIQ at the Anthropic Hackathon · APA 2026 poster on ChatGPT vs human researchers · EV driving range predicted with R² = 0.918
Known bug: Overfits to hard problems.
Open to: ML / AI engineering roles and research collaborations

ClinIQ. Helps doctors at under-resourced clinics decide which patients to see first. Ranks patients with a simple, transparent point score. A local AI model then writes a summary for the doctor and a plain-language one for the patient, answering only from a medical encyclopedia and FDA drug labels. A three-step check flags unsafe prescriptions. Built at the Anthropic Hackathon (Health & Wellbeing track). If the medical knowledge base is missing, the AI features turn off. Tags: Document search (RAG), Local AI models, Safety checks, Tool-using AI, Data pipelines.

A Value-at-Risk report for a simulated $10B bank. The AI provides one score, and everything else is standard math. Tags: AI APIs (Claude, GPT), Simulation, Classic ML, Safety checks.

chunks.source: Inductive bias · Limit what the AI controls
chunks.text: Limit what the AI controls. In my finance model, Claude contributes one number on a 1–10 scale. Everything else is standard math that can be checked.

chunks.source: Inductive bias · Keep important decisions simple
chunks.text: Keep important decisions simple. ClinIQ ranks patients with a point score anyone can audit; the AI only writes the summaries.
Fall back safely. If an AI answer can't be read or checked, the system uses a safe default instead. This page's weekly update works this way.
